nodes.name: Dummy head node
nodes.description: Put a dummy node before the head so inserts and deletes at the head need no special case; return dummy->next.

facets.recognize: Uses a dummy node whenever the head itself may change.
facets.implement: Builds from dummy and returns dummy->next.

misconceptions.desc: Returned the dummy node instead of dummy->next.
Wrote separate head-handling branches a dummy node would remove, and got one wrong.

nodes.name: Reversing a linked list
nodes.description: Walk with prev, curr and next and flip each link; recursively, reverse the rest and attach the current node at its end.

facets.recognize: Reverses by relinking instead of copying values out and back.
facets.explain: Explains what prev, curr and next hold at every step.
facets.implement: Saves next before flipping, and returns prev as the new head.
facets.trace: Can show the three pointers after each step.
facets.adapt: Reverses a sub-range or groups of k and reconnects them to the rest of the list.

misconceptions.desc: Changed curr->next before saving the next node.
Returned curr (nullptr) or the old head instead of prev.
In the recursive version, did not set head->next = nullptr, leaving a cycle.
After reversing a part (k-group, sublist), did not reconnect it to the nodes before and after.
Copied values into an array or stack and wrote them back instead of relinking.

nodes.name: Fast and slow pointers
nodes.description: Move one pointer twice as fast: they meet inside a cycle, and slow is at the middle when fast reaches the end. A gap of n nodes finds the nth from the end.

facets.recognize: Uses two speeds for middle, cycle detection, cycle start and nth from end.
facets.explain: Explains why the pointers meet in a cycle and why resetting one to the head finds the cycle start.
facets.implement: Checks fast and fast->next before each double step.
facets.adapt: Chooses the first or second middle as required; measures loop length; deletes the nth node from the end with a dummy.

misconceptions.desc: Advanced fast without checking both fast and fast->next.
Returned the first middle where the second was required (or the reverse) on an even-length list.
Cannot explain why moving one pointer back to the head finds where the cycle starts.
Counted the loop length from the wrong node or stopped one step early.
Stored visited nodes in a set (O(n) space) where two pointers give O(1).
Made the gap n - 1 or n + 1, so the wrong node was removed from the end.

nodes.name: Merging and sorting linked lists
nodes.description: Merge sorted lists by relinking nodes; sort a list with merge sort: find the middle, split, sort both halves, merge.

facets.recognize: Picks merge sort for lists (no random access, O(1) extra merge).
facets.implement: Splits at the middle, merges with a dummy and attaches the leftover list.
facets.adapt: Merges along a second pointer (flattening) and clears the pointer the result does not use.

misconceptions.desc: Did not cut the list at the middle (mid->next = nullptr), so the recursion never ended.
Forgot to attach the leftover list after one list ran out.
Copied the values into an array and sorted them (O(n) space).
When flattening, did not clear the pointer the merged list no longer uses.

nodes.name: Relinking nodes into groups
nodes.description: Build separate chains (odd and even positions, 0s/1s/2s, the pieces of a rotation) from existing nodes, then join the chains.

facets.implement: Builds each chain from a dummy, joins them in order and ends the last chain with nullptr.
facets.trace: Can show each chain after every node.
facets.adapt: Applies the same idea to rotation (close into a ring, cut at the right spot) and k-group reversal.

misconceptions.desc: Did not set the last node's next to nullptr, leaving a cycle.
Joined the chains in the wrong order, or broke when one chain was empty.
Rewrote node values where the problem asked for nodes to be relinked.
Rotated by k without reducing k modulo the list length.

nodes.name: Digit arithmetic on lists
nodes.description: Add numbers stored as digit lists, carrying from node to node; reverse (or recurse) first when the most significant digit comes first.

facets.implement: Adds digit by digit with a carry, continuing while either list or the carry remains.
facets.adapt: Handles most-significant-first lists by reversing or recursing.

misconceptions.desc: Dropped the final carry (999 + 1 lost its leading 1).
Stopped when the shorter list ended.
Converted the lists to integers, overflowing on long inputs.

nodes.name: Aligning two lists
nodes.description: Walk both lists and switch each pointer to the other list's head at its end; after equal distances they meet at the intersection (or both reach nullptr).

facets.explain: Explains why switching heads equalizes the distances walked.
facets.implement: Compares node addresses and stops when both pointers are equal, including both nullptr.

misconceptions.desc: Compared node values instead of node addresses.
Looped forever when the lists do not intersect.

nodes.name: Copying a list with extra pointers
nodes.description: Map each original node to its copy (hashmap), or interleave copies with originals, set the random pointers, then separate the lists.

facets.explain: Explains how the copy of any node is found from the original in O(1).
facets.implement: Sets each copy's random to the copy of the original's random and restores the original list.

misconceptions.desc: Pointed a copy's random at the original node instead of its copy.
After interleaving, did not restore the original list.
Did not handle random == nullptr.
